messages:
Nora Kim: ACME's renewal call flagged repeated 503s during their ramp. Can we make a 1-page customer checklist (snackable) for prefill + batch + streaming to share in enablement?
Diego Alvarez: Yep. Keep it bite-sized: top-5 quick fixes, 2 config examples (prefill + client timeout), 3 live checks customers can run.
Priya Singh: For telemetry make names plain: prefill_success_rate, stream_p90_ms, pending_queue_len. Customers should be able to paste these into dashboards.
Jamal Brooks: Quick fixes idea: 1) Identify top 8 prompts and one-off prefill them; 2) Set client batch size to 3; 3) Add client timeout + streaming fallback; 4) Set short cache TTLs for dynamic prompts; 5) Enable jittered prefill schedule.
Nora Kim: Love it. Add a tiny renewal-risk note: if prefill_success_rate < 60% and stream_p90_ms > 700ms for 48h, escalate to ops or request temporary warm pool.
Diego Alvarez: Example curl (one-liner) customers can copy:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme","prompts":["welcome","summary","followup"],"parallel":2}'
```
Priya Singh: Jitter pseudocode for scheduled prefill: `every 4m + rand(-30s..30s)` — keeps thundering-herd down.
Jamal Brooks: Client timeout + fallback guidance: set request timeout = 10s. If batch times out or returns 5xx, open streaming connection with max_chunk_tokens=64 and send smaller pieces. This reduces retry cost.
Diego Alvarez: Cache TTL suggestions (customer-friendly): ephemeral prompts = 5m, session templates = 1h, static templates = 12h. Batch size guidance: aim for 2-4 for 200-500ms SLO; increase to 6 only if you accept higher latency.
Priya Singh: Circuit breaker rule (simple): if 5xx rate > 4% over 10m, drop to half concurrency for 15m and alert ops. Give customers the exact numbers so they can set alarms.
Nora Kim: Color health indicator (copyable): GREEN = prefill_success_rate >= 80% AND stream_p90_ms < 400ms; AMBER = prefill_success_rate 60-80% OR stream_p90_ms 400-700ms; RED = prefill_success_rate < 60% OR stream_p90_ms > 700ms OR sustained error rate.
Jamal Brooks: I'll write a two-sentence customer email template: subject + 3 bullets + link to checklist. Keep tone: helpful, not alarmist.
Diego Alvarez: Add a one-click feedback widget idea: thumbs up / thumbs down and one-line "what changed" box. CS copies responses into renewal notes.
Priya Singh: For shared-hosted tenants include public path to request a temporary warm pool: support@redwood.ai (include tenant id, expected peak qps, start/end). For private/on-prem tenants note: open a support ticket + include env details.
OpsBot: Draft checklist uploaded to docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cs/public-prefill-checklist-draft (internal link). Remember to replace ops email with support@redwood.ai in the public copy.
Nora Kim: Next steps: Diego drafts the 1-pager, Priya prepares metric snippets and alarm numbers, Jamal writes the email template + booking link. Aim to publish to CS enablement repo by tomorrow morning.
Diego Alvarez: Will do — targeting a 300-400 word customer doc.
Priya Singh: I'll include templated Grafana alert rules customers can paste.
Jamal Brooks: Adding booking link for escalation call: https://cal.com/redwood-cs/30 — include in appendix.
Nora Kim: Great work. Keep it concise and action-first. Closing thread; will post final link here when published. :white_check_mark:
